claims.claim: Finite-horizon play is exactly represented by a perfect-recall belief-state recurrence.
claims.evidence: For a fixed remaining horizon without history-based termination, the White king square, White queen square, feasible black-square set, and remaining horizon suffice. All feasible hidden squares give the same current legal-move observation. After White moves, attacked black squares become distinct visible singleton observations, while unattacked squares form one invisible block. Because Black is fully informed, unioning all invisible replies within each observation block gives the exact adversarial successor. The repetition-aware claim separately augments this state with White-pair history. An independently written coordinate/set model checked all 144,508 invisible singleton placements, 4,046,612 offered White move paths, and 23,520 king-only evasion cases supporting the treatment of an unprotected queen capture as a White loss.
claims.search_method: Induction on the remaining White-move horizon, combined with exhaustive rule-level validation using an independently implemented coordinate/set model.

claims.claim: With draw termination suppressed, the exact worst-case capture time over all initial configurations is 23 White moves.
claims.evidence: Exact dynamic programming over all 249,984 labeled placements found 105,476 depth-1 captures, exactly 32 placements still losing at depth 22, and no placement losing at depth 23. The 32 lower-bound placements are precisely four dihedral-symmetry orbits represented by White king a1, Black king d4, and White queen b1, h2, g5, or h7. Thus both the upper bound and sharpness at 23 are independently established.
claims.witness: White king a1, White queen b1, Black king d4, with White to move and the initial black square known, is not winning within 22 White moves but is winning within 23.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive exact integer/bitset AND-OR dynamic programming over every White action, post-White observation block, adversarial Black reply, and post-Black observation; D4 canonicalization only removes symmetric duplicates.

claims.claim: Even with the source’s host-enforced repetition rule, White can guarantee capture within 28 White moves.
claims.evidence: History-aware exact strategy synthesis succeeded on four disjoint ranges covering all 18,081 non-immediate D4 classes: 4,521, 4,520, 4,520, and 4,520 successes, with no failures. Each class received its draw-suppressed optimum plus five moves, hence at most 28. The search tracks ordered White king/queen pairs at White-turn nodes and rejects an action when its resulting pair has already occurred twice. A third complete-position occurrence on either turn parity would require this forbidden third pair occurrence, so the synthesized strategies cannot trigger threefold repetition. The remaining 105,476 placements capture on move 1, and 28 is strictly below 50.
claims.witness: All 18,081 non-immediate symmetry classes were certified, including the depth-23 representative White king a1, White queen b1, Black king d4 at budget 28.
claims.search_method: Exact perfect-recall recursive strategy synthesis carrying ordered White-pair occurrence history and universally checking every indistinguishable Black-reply union, over exhaustive disjoint ranges of canonical initial classes.

target_evidence: The exact target asks whether White can guarantee capture under the source draw rules, from every source-legal distinct placement, within 50 White moves. The independent checks cover all 249,984 labeled initial placements: 105,476 capture immediately, while the other 144,508 reduce to 18,081 exhaustively certified symmetry classes. Their repetition-safe budgets are at most 28 White moves, strictly below 50. This proves the requested affirmative result at full strength. The draft's claimed FULL resolution is therefore ACCURATE, neither overstated nor understated.
checks_performed: Read only the designated source JSON and draft JSON; did not use the web, retrieval databases, treatment receipts, prior frontier runs, verification reports, or other solutions.
